message.content:
The **United States Declaration of Independence** was signed by **56 delegates** from the thirteen colonies on **August 2, 1776** (the signatures were added over the next few months). Here’s the full list of signers, grouped by the colony they represented:

| Colony | Signers |
|--------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, James Smith, George Taylor, James Wilson, George Ross, John Penn, George White, John Penn (the younger), John Penn (the elder) |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark, William Livingston, John Hart (the younger), John Hart (the elder) |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott, William Samuel Johnson |
| **Massachusetts** | John Adams, Samuel Adams, John Hancock, Joseph Warren, Paul Revere, John Hancock (the younger), John Hancock (the elder) |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll (the younger) |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, Joseph Hewes |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | George Wythe, James Monroe, Thomas Jefferson, Richard Henry Lee, Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton |
| **New York** | William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston, John Jay, George Clinton |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn (the younger) |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |

**Key figures** often highlighted include:

- **Thomas Jefferson** – Principal author of the Declaration.
- **John Hancock** – His bold signature is the most famous.
- **Benjamin Franklin** – Renowned statesman and scientist.
- **George Washington** – Though he did not sign the Declaration, he was a key leader of the Revolution.

These 56 men signed the document, making it one of the most iconic acts of collective political action in history.
